cards.text: Jesus has just set free a woman who'd been hunched over for eighteen years, and the whole crowd rejoiced (Luke 13:10-17). Then He asks, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?” I love a teacher who asks a question and then answers it, because back in the drawer NOBODY ever answered mine.

cards.question: Jesus picks something to compare the kingdom of God to. What does He reach for first?

cards.text: A mustard seed. A man tosses it into his garden, and when Matthew tells this same picture, it's the smallest of all seeds (Matthew 13:32).

cards.question: True or false: The tiny mustard seed the man tosses into his garden grows and becomes a tree.
The mustard seed has become a tree, and the birds of the air ___ in its branches.

cards.text: Here, Jesus doesn't stop to explain the tree. He just asks again, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?”

cards.question: Jesus is about to give a second picture of the kingdom of God. What does He compare it to?

cards.text: LEAVEN! Somebody takes it and mixes it into three measures of flour, and friend, now Jesus is talking my language.

cards.question: True or false: In Jesus' second picture, it's a man who takes the leaven and mixes it into the flour.
A woman mixes leaven into three measures of flour, until ___ of it is leavened.

cards.text: ALL of it, because leaven never stays in its corner, friend. It gets into every bit, the same way flour gets into my eyebrows and NEVER leaves.

cards.question: Look at both of Jesus' pictures of the kingdom of God, the mustard seed and the leaven. What happens to the thing that goes in?

answers.text: It doesn't stay the way it went in
It's left alone and nothing happens
It gets pulled out and thrown away
